summary: Full read of 20 SEC whistleblower award orders (2013-2025). Every award in them was already in cases.csv; this pass adds 13 denial rows (other claimants denied in the same orders, including related-action denials) and 1 event (2014 interpretation that sanctions 'deemed satisfied' in other authorities' actions count as collected), and suggests 26 corrections to existing award rows: notes on how each claimant qualified, reductions, waivers, insider status; fixes to notes that misstated the order (103856 printed 'approximately' not 'over'; 69749 and 76025 percentages are stated, not redacted; 104143 and 104145 have no current payment); a sanctions lower bound for 104139. No statistics or new rules in these orders beyond restatements of rules already recorded.

events.title: SEC counts sanctions 'deemed satisfied' in other agencies' actions as collected for awards
events.description: In an award order the Commission interpreted Section 21F(b)(1) so that disgorgement and interest in an SEC covered action that are deemed satisfied by payments in a civil action brought by another government authority count as collected when calculating the whistleblower award.
events.quote: to include amounts that are deemed satisfied when collected in actions brought by other governmental authorities.

gaps: Award percentages, sanctions, respondents and dates are redacted in most orders; nothing more can be taken from the documents.

suggested_corrections.value: Exchange Act Release No. 103856, File No. 2025-51. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Sept. 4, 2025). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "approximately $1,300,000" (not a lower bound); percentage redacted. Claimant did not contest. Original information caused staff to open the investigation (Rule 21F-4(c)(1)); ongoing assistance included seven interviews, identifying key witnesses and documents, and helping draft targeted information requests. The 30% presumption (Rule 21F-6(c)) did not apply because Claimant unreasonably delayed: waited 27 months after learning of the misconduct. One other claimant denied (separate row). Insider status, covered action and sanctions redacted or not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 103876, File No. 2025-52. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Sept. 5, 2025). Joint award to three Joint Claimants treated jointly as one whistleblower (information and Forms WB-APP submitted together through the same counsel); unless they request otherwise, each is paid 33.3% of the joint award. Amount as printed: "approximately $58,000 (based on current collections)"; percentage redacted. Two Joint Claimants were former employees of the Company in redacted positions and the third a former employee of an outside company; the order considered the officer/director exclusion (Rule 21F-4(b)(4)(iii)(A)) and found they were not excluded, and applied the 120-day exception (Rule 21F-4(b)(4)(v)(C)) because one had reported internally to a supervisor and the General Counsel. Tip prompted the opening of the investigation; significant ongoing assistance including an in-person meeting. Covered action and sanctions redacted.

Exchange Act Release No. 104134, File No. 2025-53. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Sept. 29, 2025). Claimant 1 as named in the order: "more than $180,000" (lower bound); percentage redacted; did not contest. Original information from independent knowledge significantly contributed; new important information, repeated contacts with staff, documents, witnesses identified. Received a slightly higher percentage than Claimant 2 because Claimant 2 delayed reporting. A third claimant was denied (separate row). Insider status, covered action and sanctions redacted or not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 104134, File No. 2025-53. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Sept. 29, 2025). Claimant 2 as named in the order: "more than $130,000" (lower bound); percentage redacted; did not contest. Contributed equally with Claimant 1 but received a slightly lower award because he/she "unreasonably delayed reporting his/her information to the Commission for approximately 15 months". A third claimant was denied (separate row). Insider status, covered action and sanctions redacted or not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 104139, File No. 2025-58. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Order (PDF)" (Sept. 30, 2025). Claimant 1: award equal to "$3.36 [redaction] million" (the redaction falls between the number and "million"); percentage redacted. Covered action: settled cease-and-desist proceedings against two respondents (redacted) ordering "more than $1 million in monetary sanctions", a civil money penalty that was the only monetary sanction and was collected in full. Tip alone caused staff to open the investigation; saved significant time and resources; ongoing assistance (witnesses, document requests). The Commission used Section 36(a) to waive the TCR filing requirements of Rules 21F-9(a)-(b) (tip emailed with perjury declaration early in the COVID-19 pandemic while mailrooms were not fully functional). Claimant 1 contested, asking that voluntary reimbursements made by a respondent before the action (after his/her internal report) be added to the award base; the Commission refused (not monetary sanctions; never granted such a request in the history of the program). Claimant 1 had reported internally first. Claimant 2 and two other claimants denied (separate rows).
Award to Claimant 1, whose tip alone opened the investigation; request to base the award also on reimbursements the respondent made before the action was refused.

Exchange Act Release No. 104142, File No. 2025-57. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Sept. 30, 2025). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "for a payout of approximately $700,000"; percentage redacted; award also applies to sanctions collected after the order. Claimant's TCRs "provided a roadmap for the investigation"; multiple helpful TCRs, an interview, and the Commission quoted [redacted] in a court filing. Claimant 2 denied (separate row). Insider status, covered action and sanctions redacted.

Exchange Act Release No. 104143, File No. 2025-60. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Sept. 30, 2025). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Percentage redacted; the award "would result in no current payment" (no collections yet). Claimant did not contest. Information substantially advanced an ongoing investigation (complicated transactions among numerous entities, key witnesses and documents, help with subpoenas and targeted requests, saved significant staff time). A second claimant denied (separate row). Insider status, covered action and sanctions redacted.

Exchange Act Release No. 104145, File No. 2025-61. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Sept. 30, 2025). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Percentage redacted; the award "would result in no current payment based on the lack of collections in the Covered Action". Tip prompted the opening of the investigation; ongoing assistance including an interview. No denials mentioned. Insider status, covered action and sanctions redacted.

Exchange Act Release No. 69749, File No. 2013-1. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (June 12, 2013). Whistleblowers awarded: 3 (Claimants #1, #2 and #3, 5% each of monetary sanctions collected, including any collected after the order; none contested). The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 5% each. award_pct is the share for each of the three claimants. Covered action: SEC v. Andrey C. Hicks and Locust Offshore Management, LLC, 1:11-cv-11888-RGS (D. Mass.), filed 26 October 2011, final judgments 20 March 2012 (default), Notice of Covered Action 2012-27 posted 3 April 2012: disgorgement and prejudgment interest of $2,512,058.39 (joint and several) plus a civil penalty of $2,512,058.39 on each defendant; amounts collected not given. Preliminary Determination 19 December 2012. Claimant #4 denied (separate row). Insider status not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 70775, File No. 2014-2. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 30, 2013). Whistleblowers awarded: 1 (Claimant #1). The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 30% ("in total") of monetary sanctions collected, including any collected after the order. Preliminary Determination 12 August 2013; Claimant #1 gave notice of not contesting on 6 September 2013. Claimant #2 denied and withdrew (separate row). Covered action, sanctions and insider status redacted or not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 72301, File No. 2014-5. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (June 3, 2014). Whistleblowers awarded: 2 (Claimants #1 and #2, acting in concert; 15% each, 30% in total). The order gives no dollar amount. award_pct is the total for both claimants. Preliminary Determination 7 April 2014; neither contested. Part of the disgorgement and prejudgment interest was deemed satisfied by payments in a civil action brought by another (redacted) authority and is included in the award calculation (footnote 1). Covered action, sanctions and insider status redacted or not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 72652, File No. 2014-6. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (July 22, 2014). Whistleblowers awarded: 3 (Claimant #1 15%, Claimant #2 10%, Claimant #3 5%; 30% in total). The order gives no dollar amount. award_pct is the total. Preliminary Determination 7 April 2014; Claimants #2 and #3 gave notice of not contesting (21 and 28 April 2014); Claimant #1 did not respond in time. Covered action, sanctions and insider status redacted or not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 76000, File No. 2015-7. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Sept. 28, 2015). Whistleblowers awarded: 2 (Claimant 1 11%, Claimant 2 9%; 20% in total). The order gives no dollar amount. award_pct is the total. Preliminary Determination 5 June 2015; neither contested. Covered action, sanctions and insider status redacted or not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 76025, File No. 2015-8. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Sept. 29, 2015). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 28% ("twenty-eight (28%)") of monetary sanctions collected, including any collected after the order. Preliminary Determination 13 July 2015; not contested (notice 19 August 2015). Covered action, sanctions and insider status redacted or not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 80115, File No. 2017-7. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Feb. 28, 2017). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 20%. Award reduced below what it might otherwise have been because of the claimant's culpability in the violations and unreasonable delay in reporting. Preliminary Determination 15 June 2016; not contested. Covered action and sanctions redacted.
Award to a whistleblower who was culpable in the violations and delayed reporting; both reduced the award.

Exchange Act Release No. 88687, File No. 2020-16. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (April 20, 2020). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 30%; "lack of collections in this matter" counted in the claimant's favour. Claimant reported internally to a (redacted) party, which sent a written tip to the Commission; staff opened the investigation on it (Rule 21F-4(c)(3), internal reporting route); Claimant relayed the same information by phone the next day, before the whistleblower rules took effect (12 Aug 2011). The Commission waived the "in writing" requirement of Rule 21F-9(d) under Section 36(a). Covered action concerned an ongoing fraudulent scheme. Second claimant denied (separate row). Not contested.
Award to a whistleblower who reported internally; the entity's tip opened the investigation, and the Commission waived the written-tip requirement.

Exchange Act Release No. 89354, File No. 2020-25. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (July 21, 2020). Whistleblowers awarded: 1; the claimant's estate gave notice of not contesting. The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 20%. Expeditious, specific tip with corroborating documents about an ongoing fraud prompted the investigation, stopped the fraud and returned money to investors; low collections; claimant could not keep assisting. Related-action claim for another authority's actions denied (separate row). Covered action, sanctions and insider status redacted or not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 89355, File No. 2020-24. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (July 21, 2020). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 30%; "there are currently no collections in this matter". Expeditious detailed tip with corroborating documents on an ongoing fraud the Commission did not know of prompted the investigation; continued helpful information. Not contested. No denials. Covered action, sanctions and insider status redacted or not stated.

Exchange Act Release No. 90189, File No. 2021-1. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 15, 2020). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than $800,000": lower bound; percentage redacted. The CRS had preliminarily recommended denial on the ground that Claimant was not a "whistleblower"; Claimant contested and the Commission reversed and granted the award. Claimant authored a detailed analysis that alerted staff to the violations, but gave no further assistance. A separate enforcement action and a related proceeding with sanctions under $1,000,000 were treated as part of the Covered Action (same nucleus of operative facts, Rule 21F-4(d)). Covered action, sanctions and insider status redacted.
Award granted after the claimant contested a preliminary denial (that he/she was not a 'whistleblower'); detailed analysis alerted staff to the violations.

Exchange Act Release No. 90284, File No. 2021-3. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (Oct. 29, 2020). Whistleblowers awarded: 1 (Claimant 1, did not contest). Amount as printed: "over $10,000,000" ("over $10 million"): lower bound; percentage redacted. Covered action: settled administrative and cease-and-desist proceedings against a company (redacted); sanctions redacted, stated as fully collected. Claimant 1 raised concerns internally first, then reported to the SEC when the company would not remedy; the tip caused staff to open the investigation and led to almost every finding and charge; communicated over a dozen times; law enforcement interest very high. A state agency also sued and settled with the company (not a related action). Claimants 2 and 3 and four other individuals denied (separate rows).
Award of over $10 million to a whistleblower who reported internally first and whose tip opened the investigation; six other claimants denied.
